cards.explanation: The answer is the one whose transgressions are forgiven. David says, "Blessed is he whose transgressions are forgiven…" The blessing goes to the forgiven one. That's good news for anybody who has ever scorched a whole tray and had to face the family. I'd take forgiven over flawless any day, friends.

The answer is True. David says, "Blessed is the man whose iniquity the LORD does not count against him, in whose spirit there is no deceit." So the blessed man is the forgiven one, and there's no deceit in his spirit. I think that sets up everything David says next, friends.

The answer is that he groaned all day long. David says, "When I kept silent, my bones became brittle from my groaning all day long." The silence didn't bring him peace. It came with groaning, and all day long at that. I think anybody who has carried something around and refused to say it out loud knows that ache.

The answer is False. David says, "For day and night Your hand was heavy upon me; my strength was drained as in the summer heat." Drained is about as far from "just fine" as you can get. I think this part of the psalm is heavy, so let's give it room, friends.

The answer is hide. David says, "Then I acknowledged my sin to You and did not hide my iniquity." The silence is over. He stops keeping it under wraps and brings it out to the LORD. Friends, that's the turn in the whole psalm.

The answer is that He forgives the guilt of his sin. David says, "I will confess my transgressions to the LORD…" and then he tells Him, "…You forgave the guilt of my sin." Friends, look at the order. He confesses, and forgiveness is right there. After all that groaning, I think that's the best line in the psalm.

The answer is to pray to the LORD while He may be found. David says, "Therefore let all the godly pray to You while You may be found." He's turning his own story into an invitation for everyone godly. Pray, friends, and don't put it off.

The answer is True. David says, "Surely when great waters rise, they will not come near." Great waters can rise, and still they will not come near. I'd say that's a mighty comforting picture, friends.

The answer is deliverance. David tells the LORD, "You protect me from trouble; You surround me with songs of deliverance." I picture a whole choir around him, friends. Not a bad crowd to have in your corner.

The answer is understanding. David says, "Do not be like the horse or mule, which have no understanding; they must be controlled with bit and bridle to make them come to you." Right after the line, "I will instruct you and teach you the way you should go…" this is the warning (Psalm 32:8). I think it's an invitation to listen and follow close, friends.

The answer is False. The psalm says, "Many are the sorrows of the wicked, but loving devotion surrounds him who trusts in the LORD." The wicked have many sorrows, and the verse sets that against the one who trusts. Two paths, side by side, friends.

The answer is loving devotion. The psalm says, "…loving devotion surrounds him who trusts in the LORD." Surrounds, friends, like it's packed in all the way around. Like a cookie box with no empty corners.

The answer is to be glad and shout for joy. David ends with, "Be glad in the LORD and rejoice, O righteous ones; shout for joy, all you upright in heart." The man who groaned all day long now calls everyone to shout for joy. Go ahead, friends, and make some noise.
